answer: Cheap keys used to file for irrigation rights and vote as if they ran real intakes. A right starts only after the claimant packs a hollow weir with 41 grit bags, each a 64-byte hash posted within 8 minutes, and locks 28 POA for 11 epochs. Peers walk the canyon flume, recount the bags, and void the right if any bag is missing or the pack finishes after minute 8. A river schedule then releases 7 POA after epoch 4 and the rest only after epoch 11; a short pack slashes 14 POA and zeros vote weight. Cloning 60 keys idles 1,680 POA and 2,460 bags; a missed bag cannot be reused later.
